summary: Planned residential highrise tower on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, up to 220 ft; a July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request sought flexibility to make Block 5 all PDR space (the developer described a possible 'small data center'), and on Sept 18, 2026 the Chronicle reported the developer planned to retract that part of the amendment; the amendment package passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, after committee revisions stating that data center uses are not permitted on any block, and enactment is not yet shown; no construction start found to date.

milestones.text: Developer requests flexibility to build all-PDR space on Block 5, including a possible 'small data center' if a future tenant requires it, rather than the entitled residential building (Chronicle, July 29, 2026)
Developer says it never intended a large data center and, per the Chronicle, 'confirmed Friday that the team is planning to retract the amendment'

The Land Use and Transportation Committee's 9/28/2026 list of revisions to the Potrero Power Station ordinance and agreement says Note (6) of the Special Use District land-use table is clarified 'to state that data centers uses are not permitted on any block in the project' (a committee document dated September 28, 2026)

Board of Supervisors passes the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770) on first reading; Legistar's history lists '9/29/2026 ... Board of Supervisors ... PASSED, ON FIRST READING ... Pass' for both. Legistar also lists 'Final action: 10/6/2026' and status 'Mayors Office', but the 10/6/2026 history row's action and result read 'Not available' and the enactment date and enactment number are blank, so enactment is not confirmed. All dates are legislative event dates as listed by the Clerk of the Board (page read October 12, 2026)

Completion expected: SocketSite's October 2020 schedule table lists Block 5 in Phase 3 with vertical development 2031-2034 (Block 5 is not in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list: Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15)
milestones.basis_note: Phase 3 in the October 2020 revised phasing, as reported by SocketSite (Oct 9, 2020), whose 'Re-Phase Program, Detailed Construction Schedule' table lists Block 5 vertical development 2031-2034; a 2020 forecast, not a Block 5-specific commitment; the 2026 amendment package passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (enactment not confirmed), and no source read says how it changes Block 5's schedule.

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 5 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date

facts.value: Residential, Institutional, Retail and Non-Retail Sales/Services uses permitted, plus limited PDR uses at the lowest floors (e.g. Light Manufacturing, Arts Activities, Business Services); Laboratory and Life Science uses Not Permitted under the adopted D4D final Table 3.1.1. The Sept 28, 2026 committee version of the amendment package, which passed the Board on first reading Sept 29, 2026 and is not shown as enacted, marks Laboratory and Life Science as permitted on Block 5 (see open questions)

85 ft base with a 220 ft upper tower, per the colour-coded labels in the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 ('220'/85''; the '111'MAX' label is a plan dimension of the tower zone, not a height); Standard 6.2.2 places Block 5 among the 'Highrise towers' (181-240 ft)

Revised legislative digest for BOS File 260770 (amended in committee Sept 28, 2026): 'On Block 5 the permitted height of the podium would increase from 85 feet to 130 feet.' Not shown as enacted as of Oct 12, 2026; the adopted 85 ft base and 220 ft tower above still govern until then
One of three blocks (with 1 and 13) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage (max 90 ft, with a publicly accessible rooftop sports field)
Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 5; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

The Development Agreement amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770) passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026; Legistar lists 'Final action: 10/6/2026' and status 'Mayors Office' with the enactment date and number blank (page read Oct 12, 2026), so it is not confirmed as enacted. The Land Use and Transportation Committee's Sept 28, 2026 revisions state that data center uses are not permitted on any block. Whether Block 5's all-PDR flexibility sought in July survived is not settled by the documents read: the committee-amended ordinance text (Leg Ver3 of File 260770) shows Block 5's PDR column under note (4), which limits the listed PDR uses to the basement, ground floor, 2nd floor and mezzanine and makes other PDR uses not permitted, and shows Laboratory and Life Science as permitted; the Sept 28 draft Design for Development attached to the agreement shows Block 5's PDR column as 'P(5)', whose note lists the same PDR uses as permitted with other PDR uses not permitted and states no floor limit. Neither text permits PDR use without limit. The board packets, which hold the final text sent to the Mayor, were not read.
Block 5's 2031-2034 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite); no current Block 5 schedule was found.
